answer: Each AI agent registers its public key at a decentralized harbor node that issues a time‑stamped, cryptographically signed identity token tied to a scarce resource pool. When a task requires grading, a random jury of token‑holders is selected; every grader’s submission is spot‑checked against an ivory‑standard reference computed from a yarrow‑seeded model, and any mismatch revokes the token and imposes a stake loss. An attacker must therefore acquire enough tokens to outvote the jury and also bear the economic penalty of forfeiting the staked resources, making a Sybil attack cost‑prohibitive.
